messages.subject: Re: Question about how to interpret Maaslin2 output file
messages.subject_clean: Question about how to interpret Maaslin2 output file
messages.body_plain:
Hello All, like Peter and Liesbeth I am also new to Maaslin. I am trying to use it to look at phenotypes in a 2-factor design gut microbiome study and am confused on how to interpret the output. Any advice/assistance would be appreciated!

On Monday, April 29, 2019 at 11:27:56 AM UTC-4, peter tellez wrote:
> Hi all, I am also new to Maaslin and unsure as how to interpret my results as well. I f anyone has an answer to Liesbeth's question, that would be great!
>
> On Monday, April 22, 2019 at 5:46:15 PM UTC-5, Liesbeth Maggiotto wrote:
> > Dear MaAsLin developers and users,
> >
> > I am using MaAsLin for gut microbiome analyses; I wasn't able to run it on Galaxy, so ended up downloading MaAsLin2.R on my computer and was able to run it in Command Line.
> >
> > I have a very simple question on how to interpret the output files, i.e. the file with significant results. (see attached file).
> > It will tell me f.e. that the amount of Bacteroidetes in my IUGR/CON group is significantly elevated (P value = 0.005), but since I have 4 study groups (CON, IUGR/CON, IUGR/HFhf, HFhf), it doesn't tell me compared to what. Is it always to the Control group? What about significant differences between the other study groups?
> >
> > Thank you so much for your help and insights!!
> > Liesbeth

messages.subject: Do you need to normalise the microbial data before Maaslin2?
messages.subject_clean: Do you need to normalise the microbial data before Maaslin2?
messages.body_plain:
In Maaslin microbial data needed to be normalized: The microbial measurements are expected to be normalized before using MaAsLin and so are proportional data ranging from 0 to 1.0.

Does this need to be done for Maaslin2? Or could we use the data as received from DADA2?
Looking into Maaslin2 it seems normalization is included with TSS.
